Account.description: An account or group in a directory or on the device.

distinguished_name.description:
The directory distinguished name, for example
`CN=Alice,OU=Staff,DC=example,DC=org`.

domain.description: The domain, or the device name for a local account.

Admin.description: An administrative action on the server (#132).

after.description: The object after the action, redacted (#228).

before.description: The object before the action, redacted (#228).

correlation_id.description: Ties together every record of one bulk operation or deployment.

object_type.description: The kind of object acted on, for example `policy` or `computer`.

AdminChannel.description: The channel an administrative action came through.

dropped_count.description:
Events dropped since the last report. Drops are always counted, never
silent.

tamper_attempts.description: Tamper attempts since the last report.

throttled_count.description: Events throttled since the last report.

Approval.description: An approval request and its decision.

duration_seconds.description: How long an approval would last, in seconds.

ApprovalChannel.description: The channel an approval was requested or decided through.

oneOf.description: An offline code read out to the user (#120, #159).

ApprovalKind.description: What an approval request asks for.

oneOf.description: A temporary override of the policy (#120).

AuditCategory.description: A category of the OS audit policy.

oneOf.description: Detailed tracking (process creation and the like).

AuditPolicy.description: A change to the OS audit policy.

category.description: The category of the changed subcategory.

changes.description: What changed, in the order the schema lists the values.

subcategory_guid.description: The changed subcategory's GUID, which identifies it.

AuditPolicyChange.description: One change to an audit policy subcategory.

misses.description: Lookups not answered from the cache.

Category.description: The broad class of an event.

oneOf.description: Loading a library into a process.
Installing or activating a packaged app.
Identity changes, such as local group membership.

new.description: The value after: for `add` and `replace` only.

old.description: The value before: for `remove` and `replace` only.

path.description: The member, as a JSON Pointer into the object.

ChangeOp.description: One kind of change in a JSON Patch-like diff.

class.description: What kind of device it is.

encryption.description: For storage: whether the contents are encrypted.

interface.description: The bus it is connected through.

product_id.description: The product ID (for USB, the 16-bit PID).

vendor_id.description: The vendor ID (for USB, the 16-bit VID).

DeviceClass.description: What kind of peripheral it is.

oneOf.description: A keyboard, mouse or other human interface device.
A phone or portable media device.

DeviceInterface.description: The bus a peripheral is connected through.

oneOf.description: An SD or other memory-card reader.

DeviceType.description: The kind of device a file is stored on.

Direction.description: Which way a connection goes, seen from the device.

oneOf.description: Between two endpoints on the device.

DnsName.description: A lowercase DNS name without a trailing dot.

duration_seconds.description: How long the grant lasts, in seconds.

request_id.description: The request it fulfils, if one was made.

token_profile.description: The token profile applied, by name.

oneOf.description: A just-in-time grant, requested and approved (#158).
The user asked for it on one application (#155).
A rule elevated the application without asking.
Palisade's replacement for the OS consent prompt (#155).

EncryptionState.description: Whether a storage device's contents are encrypted.

oneOf.description: Encryption or decryption is in progress.

EventMode.description:
The enforcement mode in effect when the event happened.

This is the policy [`Mode`] as seen by an event, plus two states the
agent can be in. [`EventMode::from_policy_mode`] converts.

oneOf.description: Decisions are evaluated and would-block decisions reported.
Like `monitor`, with a full event for every decision.
Audit, collecting would-block objects as learning candidates.
A simulation of a policy that is not deployed.

File.description: The file an event is about: the target of a decision.

ads_name.description: The alternate data stream name, if the target is a stream.

device_type.description: The kind of device the file is on.

modified.description: When the file was last modified.

owner_sid.description: The SID of the file owner.

package_name.description: For packaged apps: the package family or full name.

path.description: The path as reported, for example a device path.

path_normalised.description: The path with drive letters and `%ENV%` substitutions.

user_writable_location.description: Whether a standard user can write to the file's location.

Fim.description:
A change to a monitored file (#183). The file as it is now is
[`super::Event::file`]; this records what it was before.

old_path.description: For a rename, the path before.

watch.description: The monitoring rule that matched, by name.

FimChange.description: What happened to a monitored file.

oneOf.description: The file was renamed or moved: the old path is in `old_path`.
The file's owner or permissions changed.
The file's attributes or timestamps changed.

GroupScope.description: The scope of a security group.

oneOf.description: A group on one device, or a domain-local group.

Guid.description: A GUID in canonical lowercase form, without braces.

Hashes.description:
The digests of a file.

`sha256`, `sha1` and `md5` are flat hashes of the whole file. The
`authenticode_*` digests are the digest a signature covers: the
Authenticode image hash for PE files, or the subject-interface-package
digest for scripts and other signable formats. SHA-1 and MD5 are for
matching OS and imported data only, never the sole basis of a decision
(ADR 0008).

md5.description: MD5 of the file. Interop only.

sha1.description: SHA-1 of the file. Interop only.

oneOf.description: Working, with a problem that needs attention.

Host.description: The device an event is about.

arch.description: The CPU architecture, for example `x86_64` or `aarch64`.

domain.description: The directory domain the device is joined to.

groups.description: The device groups it belongs to, at most 64.

ips.description: The device's IP addresses, at most 32.

name.description: The host name. Dropped in anonymous mode (#228).

os.description: The operating system, for example `Windows 11 Enterprise`.

HostId.description: The ID of an enrolled device, assigned by the server at enrolment.

Identity.description:
Identity details: logons and group membership changes. The account that
logged on, or that made a change, is [`super::Event::user`].

authentication_package.description: The authentication package, for example `Kerberos` or `NTLM`.

member.description: The account added to or removed from the group.

status_code.description: For a failed logon: the OS status code (an NTSTATUS value).

sub_status_code.description: For a failed logon: the more specific OS status code.

workstation.description: The name of the workstation the logon came from.

IpAddress.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address in canonical form.

JsonValue.description: A JSON value without null or non-integer numbers. Nesting (at most 16) and size (at most 1024 values) are checked by the reader.

LanguageMode.description: The PowerShell language mode a script ran in.

LogonType.description:
How a logon session was created. The names follow the OS logon types
2 to 13.

oneOf.description: 8: from the network with a cleartext password.

Native.description:
Details from OS-native enforcement: the OS code integrity and legacy
rule-collection engines.

These are the OS's own identifiers. Linking them to the Palisade policy
and rule that produced the native policy fills [`Event::policy`] (#90).

catalog_sha1.description: The SHA-1 digest used for catalog lookup. Interop only.

catalog_sha256.description: The SHA-256 digest used for catalog lookup.

clsid.description: The COM class ID, for COM activation events.

fqbn.description:
The fully qualified binary name (publisher, product, file name and
version), verbatim.

managed_installer_enabled.description: Whether the native policy trusts files from a managed installer.

passes_managed_installer.description: Whether the file carried a managed-installer origin claim.

policy_audit_mode.description: Whether the native policy was in audit mode.

policy_count.description: How many policies an activation or refresh covered.

policy_options.description: The native policy's option bits, as the OS reports them on activation.

requested_signing_level.description: The signing level the caller requested (code 0 to 14).

rule_hash.description:
The hash the rule-collection engine computed for hash rules. Its
algorithm depends on the file type, so it is not one of [`Hashes`].

signing_scenario.description: The signing scenario: 0 for kernel mode, 1 for user mode.

status_code.description: The OS status code (an NTSTATUS value).

validated_signing_level.description: The signing level the OS validated (code 0 to 14).

protocol.description: The IP protocol number (IANA), for example 6 for TCP and 17 for UDP.

resolution.description: How `remote_hostname` was learned. Present only with it.

unc.description: The UNC path requested, for example `\\files\share\a.exe`.

ObjectType.description: The class of object being evaluated. Scripts are `script.<kind>`.

motw_zone.description: The zone in the file's mark of the web.

oneOf.description: The action was allowed, but would have been blocked if enforced.
The action ran with elevated rights.
The user or the system cancelled the action.
Information only: no allow or block decision.

ParentProcess.description:
A parent process. It has no parent of its own: the grandparent is
summarised on the child.

cmdline.description:
The command line. Collected only when permitted, and redacted by
default (#228).

image_path.description: The image path as reported, for example a device path.

image_path_normalised.description: The image path with drive letters and `%ENV%` substitutions.

owner_sid.description: The SID of the process owner.

process_key.description:
A key that identifies the process uniquely on the device, assigned
by the agent's process tracker (#59). Process IDs are reused; this is not.

PolicyId.description: The stable ID of a policy.

PolicyRef.description: The Palisade policy and rule behind a decision.

hash.description: The SHA-256 of the policy bundle.

profile_id.description: The profile the policy was assigned through.

rule_type.description: The kind of rule, for example `hash`, `publisher` or `path`.

Principal.description: Who acted, as the server knows them.

id.description:
The principal's stable ID: a user ID, an API token or client ID, or
a job name.

sid.description: The Windows security identifier, for directory accounts.

upn.description: The user principal name or e-mail address.

PrincipalKind.description: Who acted: a person, a client or a component.

oneOf.description: A person signed in to the console or a client.
An API client, identified by its token or client ID.
An operator of the Palisade instance, outside the tenant.

Probe.description: One compliance probe and its result (#210).

control.description: The control it evidences, for example `ISM-1623`.

detail.description: A short explanation of the result.

id.description: The probe's stable ID, for example `powershell_script_block_logging`.

observed.description: The value found on the device.

ProbeStatus.description: The result of a compliance probe.

oneOf.description: The device does not meet the requirement.
The requirement does not apply to this device.

cmdline.description:
The command line. Collected only when permitted, and redacted by
default (#228).

grandparent.description: A summary of the grandparent process.

image_path.description: The image path as reported, for example a device path.

image_path_normalised.description: The image path with drive letters and `%ENV%` substitutions.

owner_sid.description: The SID of the process owner.

parent.description: The parent process, with the same fields.

process_key.description:
A key that identifies the process uniquely on the device, assigned
by the agent's process tracker (#59). Process IDs are reused; this is not.

ProcessSummary.description: A short description of a process.

default_value.description:
The value is the key's unnamed (default) value. Never with a
`value_name`.

value_name.description:
The value's name. The unnamed (default) value has no name: it is
recorded with `default_value` instead.

RegistryData.description:
Registry value data: recorded truncated, hashed, or both, never in full
beyond the preview limit.

preview.description:
The data as text: strings as they are, numbers in decimal, a list of
strings joined with line feeds, anything else as lowercase hex. At
most 1024 characters.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the data's raw bytes.

size.description: The size of the data in bytes.

truncated.description: The preview is shorter than the data. Only with a `preview`.

RegistryKey.description: A registry key path: the full root key name, then components of 1 to 255 characters separated by `\`.

RegistryOperation.description: What was done to a registry key or value.

oneOf.description: A key's values or subkeys were read.

RegistryValueType.description: The type of registry value data. The names follow the OS value types.

oneOf.description: A string with unexpanded environment variables.

ResolutionMethod.description: How a remote host name was learned.

oneOf.description: A DNS query the agent observed.
A reverse lookup of the remote address.
The name the application asked for, before resolution.

Restriction.description:
A restriction a script interpreter applied, or in audit mode would have
applied, because the script is not allowed to run unrestricted.

error_id.description: The interpreter's identifier for the restriction.

language_mode.description: The language mode that applies, or would apply.

message.description: The interpreter's message, with the script position.

title.description: The kind of restriction, as the interpreter titles it.

RuleId.description: The stable ID of a rule. It is never reused, even after the rule is deleted.

SchemaVersion.description: A semantic version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, without pre-release or build suffixes.

Script.description:
A script.

A script is either a file (`path`) or inline text (`inline: true`):
exactly one of the two.
A file-backed script's digests and signatures are in [`Event::file`].

amsi_content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the content passed to the antimalware scan interface.

inline.description:
The script was inline text, not a file.

Writers leave it out when it is not set. Readers also accept an
explicit `false`, as 1.0 did, so this flag alone keeps two spellings
until the next major version. The flags added in 1.1 accept only
`true`.

language_mode.description: The language mode it ran in.

text.description:
The script text as the interpreter logged it. Collected only when
permitted, and redacted by default, like the command line (#228).
Since 1.1.

oneOf.description: `.js`, `.jse` run by the OS script host.

Sid.description: A Windows security identifier in its canonical text form.

Signer.description:
One signature on a file, leaf first.

`signature_type`, `signing_level` and `verification_error` keep the OS
codes as numbers, so values the decoder tables (#90) do not know yet are
not lost.

issuer_tbs_hash.description: The hash of the issuing certificate's to-be-signed part.

publisher.description: The leaf certificate's subject common name.

signature_type.description: How the OS verified the signature (code 0 to 7).

signing_level.description: The signing level the OS validated (code 0 to 14).

tbs_hash.description: The hash of the leaf certificate's to-be-signed part.

timestamp.description: The signing time from a trusted timestamp.

verification_error.description: Why verification failed, or 0 if it succeeded (code 0 to 28).

Source.description: The log an event was translated from.

activity_id.description: The source's correlation activity ID, which groups related records.

format.description:
For `third_party`: the generic name of the import format, for
example `generic`. Present exactly when `kind` is `third_party`.
Since 1.1.

rule_name.description:
The rule or policy that decided, as the source names it. For events
imported from another product, whose rules have no Palisade ID.
Since 1.1.

SourceKind.description: A kind of log that events can be translated from.

oneOf.description:
Events imported from another product, in a generic format named by
`source.format`. Since 1.1.

Timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 UTC timestamp with exactly six fractional digits and `Z`.

TokenElevationType.description: The elevation type of a process token.

oneOf.description: No split token (UAC off, or a built-in or service account).
The elevated half of a split token.
The filtered half of a split token.

User.description: The user an event is about.

elevated.description: Whether the acting token was elevated.

is_admin.description: Whether the user is a local administrator.

logon_id.description: The logon ID (locally unique identifier) of the logon session.

name.description: The account name. Dropped or pseudonymised by redaction (#228).

session_id.description: The logon session's terminal-services session ID.

Uuid7.description: A UUID version 7 in canonical lowercase form.

VersionInfo.description: The version resource of a PE file.

Zone.description: The security zone a file was downloaded from (its mark of the web).

description:
One canonical event.

Field order here is the serialisation order, so [`Event::to_canonical_json`]
is deterministic.

audit_policy.description: The OS audit policy change. Since 1.1.

category.description: The type's category. It must match the registry.

clock_skew_ms.description: The producer's last measured clock offset, in milliseconds.

clock_synced.description: Whether the producer's wall clock was synchronised when `ts` was taken.

description.description: A human-readable description of the event (ISM-0585).

event_id.description: A unique ID, assigned by the producer.

host.description: The device the event is about (ISM-0585: IT equipment).

identity.description: Logon and group membership details. Since 1.1.

mode.description: The enforcement mode, where one applies.

network.description: The network connection or request. Since 1.1.

policy.description: The Palisade policy and rule that decided, if known.

prev_hash.description:
The chain value of the producer's previous event. Absent only when
`seq` is 0.

registry.description: The registry key or value. Since 1.1.

schema_version.description: The schema version of this event.

seq.description: The producer's sequence number, starting at 0.

severity.description: 0 to 10. See [`Severity::syslog`] for the syslog mapping.

source.description: Where the event came from, for events translated from another log.

ts.description: When the event happened, in UTC.

ts_agent_monotonic.description:
The producer's monotonic clock when the event was recorded, in
microseconds since the agent started. It orders events even when the
wall clock jumps.
